authority.statement: The notice and locator grant no permission or authority.

boundaries: BTE remains non-admitting; this notice supports no completeness, profile, catalogue, release, deployment, or production promotion claim.
Do not treat command existence or development-only 13/16 mechanics as admitted completeness.
Do not rewrite historical audits, manifests, or receipts; publish new current evidence or append-only supersession only after authorization.
Do not merge, retire, rename, or mark EVF superseded without a separate owner decision and reference-migration evidence.
Do not copy private DomainSpec material into public Arcanum packages or fixtures.
This notice is communication evidence only and grants no implementation, routing, Git, publication, release, or external-delivery authority.
key_points: On current origin/master, the supported profile still pins a stale kinds digest, while its relationships digest now matches authority. The remaining kinds mismatch is sufficient for the minted-project compiler to stop with REGISTRY_DIGEST_MISMATCH before its intended checks run.

The profile declares JSON formation schemas for Entity, Event, Operation, and Rule, but the compiler validates through another route and discards base-schema body violations; an invalid Entity was accepted by that route.

BTE producer identity is optional, so implementation/expectation separation can be omitted; verify:bte:contracts currently runs prepared tests rather than validating the governed freezes and emitting a bound receipt.
Binding resolution accepts an empty selector, returns the first match, and carries none of the governing profile, schema, criterion, fixture, adapter, or evaluator digests.

Package scripts expose verify:bte commands that the BTE Work Pack still marks planned. On current origin/master, 38 of 61 files in the historical July review manifest remain byte-identical; the old audit remains historical evidence, not current readiness.
Proposed ownership boundary: keep EVF as design, decisions, and history; make BTE the exclusive owner of executable completeness and current readiness. This proposal is not yet an accepted decision.
The review did not support merging, retiring, renaming, or marking EVF superseded without a separate owner decision and migration evidence.

next_actions.action: Resolve the six open calls and name accountable profile, formation, validation, binding, and readiness owners.
After authorization, atomically rebind registry digests and regenerate only governed dependent fixtures and receipts, then replay focused compiler/view checks.
Record the sole admitted formation route or an exact compatibility/retirement transition before changing compiler enforcement.
Freeze expected inputs and producer identities independently from the implementation lane.
Make producer identity mandatory and provide a live verifier that consumes governed freezes and emits a replayable bound receipt.
Replace empty and first-match resolution with exact, unique, digest-bound matching and reason-specific negative tests.
Reconcile command status with package scripts and publish current readiness evidence without altering historical bytes.

open_calls.question: Confirm or reject the proposed boundary: EVF owns design/history and BTE exclusively owns executable completeness and current readiness.
Authorize an atomic profile-registry rebind, including affected fixtures and expected receipts, and name the accountable profile/compiler owner.
Choose the formation transition: enforce both declared JSON schemas and current criteria until a versioned successor exists, or approve an explicit compatibility/retirement route.
Confirm mandatory registry-resolved producer identity and nominate independent validation and implementation owners.
Confirm fail-closed binding semantics: nonempty role-typed selector, governing digests, and exactly one compatible result.
Name the owner for a current BTE readiness manifest that separates command existence, stage, admission, platform, subject digests, results, and receipts.

source_refs.label: Pinned registry bindings, declared formation schemas, and non-admitted experimental profile.
Formation route, registry-digest rejection, and discarded body violations.
Optional producer identities and conditional self-authorship rejection.
Digest-free empty-selector and first-match binding behavior.
Owner-gated non-admitting state and planned command table.
Historical pending snapshot whose bytes do not represent current readiness.

payload.subject: Confirm EVF/BTE ownership and prioritize five verified repairs
payload.why_now: An adversarial EVF/BTE review reduced fifteen provisional concerns to five verified defects. Two block or invalidate the current minted-project compiler path; three weaken validation independence, binding correctness, and operational readiness. Owner decisions are required before repair work is routed or any completeness claim is made.
